name: Madrid
intro: Spain's capital: three great art museums on one avenue, a royal palace, a huge park and late-night tapas. Compact centre with an excellent metro.
sources: Written from general knowledge for the MVP; needs a human review before launch

areas.name: Sol & Plaza Mayor
areas.blurb: The old centre around kilometre zero.

areas.name: Royal Palace & Templo de Debod
areas.blurb: Palace, cathedral and the sunset temple.

areas.name: Prado & Paseo del Arte
areas.blurb: The Prado, Reina Sofía and Thyssen on one boulevard.

areas.name: Retiro Park
areas.blurb: Madrid's great park with a boating lake.

areas.name: La Latina & Lavapiés
areas.blurb: Tapas streets and the Sunday flea market.

areas.name: Gran Vía & Malasaña
areas.blurb: Big avenue, theatres and lively squares.

areas.name: Santiago Bernabéu
areas.blurb: The Real Madrid stadium in the north.

pois.name: Prado Museum
pois.costNote: Free in the last two opening hours
pois.why: One of the world's great art museums: Velázquez's Las Meninas, Goya and Bosch.
pois.kid: Find the tiny painter hiding in Las Meninas (it's Velázquez himself).
pois.tip: Free entry in the last two hours of the day; the queue starts early.

pois.name: Reina Sofía Museum
pois.why: Modern art museum with Picasso's Guernica.
pois.kid: Guernica is huge: count the animals in the painting.
pois.tip: Free in the evenings on most days; check the site.

pois.name: Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum
pois.why: A private collection that runs from medieval art to Pop Art.

pois.name: Cibeles Palace viewpoint
pois.why: The wedding-cake city hall; its rooftop terrace looks down the grand avenues.
pois.kid: Wave to the goddess Cibeles in her lion-drawn chariot below.

pois.name: CaixaForum vertical garden
pois.why: A wall covered in 15,000 living plants beside a floating brick building.
pois.kid: How many different shades of green can you count?

pois.name: Retiro Park & boating lake
pois.why: Madrid's great park: row a boat on the lake below the colonnade monument.
pois.kid: Row a boat and watch for the turtles on the lake edge.
pois.tip: Boats are cheapest on weekday mornings.

pois.name: Palacio de Cristal
pois.why: A glass-and-iron pavilion beside a pond in the Retiro.
pois.kid: Look for the ducks and turtles in the pond outside.

pois.name: Puerta de Alcalá
pois.why: A granite city gate from 1778 at the corner of the Retiro.

pois.name: Royal Palace
pois.why: Western Europe's largest royal palace by floor area, with 3,000+ rooms.
pois.kid: Find the Stradivarius violins and the armour for kids in the Royal Armoury.
pois.tip: Free for EU residents late in the afternoon on some days; check the site.

pois.name: Almudena Cathedral
pois.why: The cathedral facing the palace, with a colourful painted ceiling.

pois.name: Plaza de Oriente
pois.why: Formal gardens with statues of old kings in front of the palace.

pois.name: Templo de Debod
pois.why: A real Egyptian temple, gifted to Spain and rebuilt in a park. Best at sunset.
pois.kid: This temple is over 2,000 years old and came from Egypt by ship.

pois.name: Teleférico cable car
pois.why: A cable car over the trees to the Casa de Campo park.
pois.tip: Runs on a reduced schedule in winter.

pois.name: Plaza Mayor
pois.why: The grand arcaded square of old Madrid, once used for bullfights and festivals.
pois.kid: Find the painted figures on the Casa de la Panadería façade.
pois.tip: Have a drink one street away; the square's cafés are pricey.

pois.name: Mercado de San Miguel
pois.why: An iron-and-glass market hall full of tapas counters.
pois.tip: Busy and not cheap; nice for a taste.

pois.name: Puerta del Sol
pois.why: The busy square at kilometre zero of Spain's roads.
pois.kid: Find the bear and strawberry tree statue, the city's symbol, and stand on the km 0 plaque.

pois.name: Chocolatería San Ginés
pois.why: Since 1894: churros dipped in thick hot chocolate.
pois.kid: Dip your churro and race to finish before the chocolate cools.

pois.name: Gran Vía
pois.why: Madrid's Broadway: early 20th-century buildings, theatres and shops.
pois.kid: Look up at the Metrópolis building's winged statue.

pois.name: Plaza del Dos de Mayo
pois.why: A neighbourhood square in Malasaña with a playground and café terraces.

pois.name: El Rastro flea market
pois.why: Madrid's huge Sunday-morning street market.
pois.kid: Hunt for old comics and toys.
pois.tip: Sunday and public holiday mornings only; mind your bags.

pois.name: Madrid Río park
pois.why: A long riverside park with playgrounds and bridges.

pois.name: Santiago Bernabéu stadium tour
pois.why: The Real Madrid stadium tour: pitch-side view, trophy room and changing rooms.
pois.kid: Count the European Cups in the trophy room.

pois.name: Cava Baja tapas street
pois.why: La Latina's tapas street; go bar to bar for small plates.
pois.tip: Busiest on Sunday after the Rastro.

pois.name: Casa Labra
pois.why: An old tavern near Sol famous for cod croquettes and fritters.

pois.name: Barrio de las Letras tapas
pois.why: Literary quarter between Sol and the Prado, full of tapas bars.

pois.name: Mercado de San Antón
pois.why: A modern market in Chueca with food stalls and a rooftop terrace.

dayTrips.name: Toledo
dayTrips.from: High-speed Avant train from Madrid Atocha, then bus or walk up
dayTrips.why: A walled hill city of churches, synagogues and mosques above a river gorge.
highlights: Synagogue of Santa María la Blanca
dayTrips.tip: Book the Avant train ahead. Wear good shoes: the streets are steep.

dayTrips.name: Segovia
dayTrips.from: High-speed train from Madrid Chamartín to Segovia AV, then bus to the aqueduct
dayTrips.why: A Roman aqueduct without mortar and a fairy-tale castle.
dayTrips.tip: Climb the Alcázar tower for the view.

dayTrips.name: El Escorial
dayTrips.from: Cercanías C8 train from Atocha or Chamartín
dayTrips.why: A vast royal monastery-palace in the mountains, with the tombs of Spanish kings.

dayTrips.name: Ávila
dayTrips.why: The best-preserved medieval walls in Spain, which you can walk on.

tips.title: Getting around
tips.text: Buy a Multi card at any metro machine and load a 10-trip ticket; one card can be shared, validating once per person. The metro is fast and air-conditioned.

tips.title: Meal times
tips.text: Lunch is late (14:00–16:00) and dinner later (from 21:00). Tapas bars fill the gap. The weekday menú del día is the best-value meal.

tips.title: Museums
tips.text: The Prado, Reina Sofía and Thyssen have free time slots; check each site. Most museums close on Monday or Tuesday.

tips.title: Heat
tips.text: July and August are very hot: plan museums for the afternoon and parks for the morning.

tips.title: Safety
tips.text: Pickpockets work Sol, the Rastro and the metro. Emergency number: 112.
